learningObjectives.title: Uses and dangers of EM waves

questions.q: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum has the longest wavelength?
questions.explain: Radio waves sit at the long-wavelength (low-frequency) end of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.q: Which type of electromagnetic wave has the highest frequency?
questions.explain: Gamma rays lie at the high-frequency, short-wavelength end of the spectrum.

questions.q: All electromagnetic waves are what type of wave?
questions.explain: Electromagnetic waves are transverse, with oscillations perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer.

questions.q: How do the speeds of the different electromagnetic waves compare when travelling in a vacuum?
options: They all travel at the same speed, 3 x 10^8 m/s
questions.explain: In a vacuum every electromagnetic wave travels at the speed of light, 3 x 10^8 m/s.

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave has a frequency of 3 x 10^9 Hz and travels at 3 x 10^8 m/s in a vacuum. What is its wavelength? (Use wavelength = speed / frequency)
questions.explain: Wavelength = 3 x 10^8 / 3 x 10^9 = 0.1 m.

questions.q: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum lies between infrared and ultraviolet?
questions.explain: In order of increasing frequency the spectrum runs infrared, visible light, then ultraviolet.

questions.q: Which group of electromagnetic waves is ionising and therefore able to damage cells?
questions.explain: The high-frequency waves ultraviolet, X-rays and gamma rays carry enough energy to ionise atoms.

questions.q: Which is a common use of microwaves?
questions.explain: Microwaves are used for satellite and mobile phone communications as well as for cooking.

questions.q: Infrared radiation is used in which of the following?
questions.explain: Infrared is emitted by warm objects, so it is used in thermal imaging and TV remote controls.

questions.q: In medicine, gamma rays are used to...
questions.explain: Gamma rays are used to treat cancer and to sterilise medical equipment.

questions.q: What is the main danger of over-exposure to ultraviolet radiation from the Sun?
questions.explain: Ultraviolet is ionising and damages skin cells, increasing the risk of skin cancer.

questions.q: Why do microwaves heat food effectively?
options: They are absorbed by water molecules in the food
They are reflected off the surface of the food
They ionise the atoms of the food
They pass straight through without any effect
questions.explain: Microwaves are absorbed by water molecules, transferring energy that heats the food.

questions.q: A hospital needs to produce an image of a patient's suspected broken bone. Which electromagnetic radiation is most suitable?
questions.explain: X-rays pass through soft tissue but are absorbed by bone, producing a clear shadow image.

questions.q: What does a convex (converging) lens do to rays of light travelling parallel to its principal axis?
options: Brings them together at the principal focus
Spreads them outwards as if from a point
questions.explain: A convex lens converges parallel rays to meet at the principal focus.

questions.q: What is the principal focus of a converging lens?
options: The point where rays parallel to the principal axis meet after passing through the lens
The exact centre of the lens
The position where the object must be placed
The outer edge of the lens
questions.explain: The principal focus is where rays parallel to the axis converge after refraction by the lens.

questions.q: An object 2 cm tall produces an image 6 cm tall through a lens. What is the magnification? (magnification = image height / object height)
questions.explain: Magnification = 6 / 2 = 3.

questions.q: When a convex lens is used as a magnifying glass, the image formed is...
questions.explain: With the object inside the focal length, a convex lens gives a virtual, upright, magnified image.

questions.q: An object is placed beyond twice the focal length of a converging lens. The image formed is...
options: Real, upright and the same size
questions.explain: Beyond 2F a converging lens forms a real, inverted image that is smaller than the object.

questions.q: What is a perfect black body?
options: An object that absorbs all the radiation that falls on it
An object that reflects all radiation
An object that can only emit radio waves
An object that cannot emit any radiation
questions.explain: A perfect black body absorbs all incident radiation and is also the best possible emitter.

questions.q: As an object becomes hotter, what happens to the electromagnetic radiation it emits?
options: It emits more radiation and the peak wavelength becomes shorter
questions.explain: Hotter bodies emit radiation at all wavelengths more intensely and the peak shifts to shorter wavelengths.
